summary: Health-probe surge and keepalive queue locking causing elevated 5xx and routing lag for Dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
BrightLaw (dedicated tenant) experienced an elevated 5xx rate and increased routing latency starting 2026-03-13 18:02 UTC. Symptoms include intermittent 502/503 responses from the API gateway, long tail request latencies, and a significant increase in backend runtime restarts. Initial triage points to a correlated spike in health-check traffic combined with keepalive connection queue locking on the gateway layer which amplified upstream backpressure and caused priority fanout saturation.

Impact:
- Customer-facing API calls returned ~8-12% 5xx rate during the 18:02–18:40 UTC window for us-east routes.
- Streaming session failures observed for ~3% of open sessions (clients saw abrupt disconnects).
- Increased CPU on ephemeral proxies and repeated runtime worker restarts causing degraded throughput for other dedicated tenants in the same shard.

Timeline (UTC):
- 18:01:36: Monitoring alert: api-gateway 5xx rate > baseline for prod-us-east.
- 18:02:10: Spike in healthprobe traffic from internal infra (control-plane) and external BrightLaw heartbeat probes.
- 18:03:00: Keepalive connection queue depth climbed > 10k, accept-queue latency rose, apigw started returning 502s.
- 18:05–18:18: Multiple serving-runtime worker restarts (nvml/gpu-driver resets correlated).
- 18:20: SRE applied temporary ingress keepalive-window tightening policy; partial stabilization.
- 18:40: Rolling firewall rule applied to rate-limit health probes from misconfigured monitoring agent for BrightLaw; 5xx rate returned toward baseline.

Steps to reproduce (how we reproduced in staging):
1) Simulate a controlled flood of short-interval health probes (1s interval) from an external IP range while maintaining a background of steady streaming traffic.
2) Configure keepalive timeouts to be long and lower the accept-queue size on a gateway replica.
3) Observe accept-queue growth, connection hold times, and prioritized request queue saturation causing 502s.

Logs / Observed traces (snippets):
- apigw: "WARN accept_queue_lag=184ms depth=10234 route=brightlaw-pri -> drop_rate=0.12"
- proxy: "ERROR keepalive_pool_lock_wait=220ms fd_inuse=918 uptime=00:12:34"
- runtime: "CRITICAL worker_pid=2241 nvml_reset=1 oom_kill=0 exit_code=137 backtrace=..."

Hypothesis / Root causes under investigation:
- A misconfigured BrightLaw monitoring agent started emitting health probes at 1s intervals to a customer route; traffic pattern caused apigw accept-queue saturation.
- Long-lived keepalive connections combined with a priority fanout policy created head-of-line blocking; slow health probe handshakes prevented garbage collection of ephemeral sockets.
- Backpressure propagated to serving runtime causing worker restarts (observed nvml resets and GPU warmup delays).

Mitigation performed so far:
- Applied immediate ingress rate-limit for healthprobe source IPs impacting BrightLaw (18:20 UTC).
- Tightened keepalive window and lowered per-replica accept-queue size temporarily to avoid large queue accumulation (18:22 UTC).
- Bounced a small subset of ephemeral proxies to clear stuck sockets and reduce fd pressure (18:25 UTC).

Current status and next steps:
- Status: partial stabilization; 5xx rate reduced to ~1.2% after mitigations but not fully back to baseline. Root cause investigation ongoing.
- SRE to run deeper socket and epoll profiling to identify lock contention hotspots (owner: Diego Martinez).
- Engineering to evaluate changes to priority fanout logic to prevent head-of-line blocking under probe-flood patterns (owner: Elena Ko).
- CS to coordinate with BrightLaw to fix the misconfigured health probe cadence and provide a recommended probe policy (owner: Maya Patel).
- Plan a targeted runtime patch to add a short-circuit path for health probe requests at the apigw level to avoid runtime fanout during probe storms.

Requested customer-facing resolution:
- Provide BrightLaw a post-incident summary, recommended probe cadence (>=15s), and temporary rollout of a per-tenant probe rate limiter.
- Offer one week of increased observability (extended traces) to validate no residual regression.

Notes:
- Related long-running ticket SUP-541213 documents a prior healthcheck spike incident; patterns partially overlap but current incident includes GPU warmup resets which were not present previously.
- No billing discrepancy reported; no data exfiltration indicators observed.
